title: AND HE SHOWED UP
description: A True Story of Faith, Family, and Finding God in the Storm What do you do when your family is thrown into a crisis you never expected and the future you trusted suddenly feels uncertain? For Jenny Beldin, life changed when a devastating accusation brought a painful investigation, separation, financial pressure, and emotional turmoil into her family’s home. As she and her husband faced an ordeal that tested their marriage, their strength, and their hope, everyday life became a struggle to keep moving forward. In And He Showed Up , Jenny shares her personal account of this difficult season, drawing readers into the fear, frustration, grief, and uncertainty she experienced along the way. From the challenges of raising adopted children and navigating family responsibilities to the strain of a prolonged investigation, she describes what it meant to keep showing up when life felt overwhelming. But this is also a story of faith. Through prayer, Scripture, the support of friends and fellow believers, and her relationship with Jesus Christ, Jenny reflects on how she found strength during moments when she could not see a clear way forward. Her experience becomes a reminder that faith is not always about having the answers it can mean trusting God one day at a time, even in the middle of the storm. Inside this heartfelt Christian memoir, you’ll discover: Faith in difficult seasons: Holding on to God when circumstances feel confusing and unfair. The power of prayer: Finding comfort and direction when words are hard to find. Family under pressure: Facing painful challenges while trying to preserve hope and connection. title: How We Show Up: Reclaiming Family, Friendship, and Community
description: An Invitation to Community and Models for Connection After almost every presentation activist and writer Mia Birdsong gives to executives, think tanks, and policy makers, one of those leaders quietly confesses how much they long for the profound community she describes. They have family, friends, and colleagues, yet they still feel like they're standing alone. They're "winning" at the American Dream, but they're lonely, disconnected, and unsatisfied. It seems counterintuitive that living the "good life"--the well-paying job, the nuclear family, the upward mobility--can make us feel isolated and unhappy. But in a divided America, where only a quarter of us know our neighbors and everyone is either a winner or a loser, we've forgotten the key element that helped us make progress in the first place: community. In this provocative, groundbreaking work, Mia Birdsong shows that what separates us isn't only the ever-present injustices built around race, class, gender, values, and beliefs, but also our denial of our interdependence and need for belonging. In response to the fear and discomfort we feel, we've built walls, and instead of leaning on each other, we find ourselves leaning on concrete. Through research, interviews, and stories of lived experience, How We Show Up returns us to our inherent connectedness where we find strength, safety, and support in vulnerability and generosity, in asking for help, and in being accountable. Showing up--literally and figuratively--points us toward the promise of our collective vitality and leads us to the liberated well-being we all want.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3"]', '#CardInstanceJTd5qw8plUXPVfCm9BM6qQ')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_Detai

title: Show Up to Win: How to Land the Leadership Role You Want
description: A USA Today Bestseller To win top leadership roles, be as skilled at your job search as you are at your job. Today, executive careers are more fluid than ever, and so is the executive job market. As an ambitious leader, you have no problem closing a deal or hitting your numbers, but knowing how to take the next step, the big step, will prove more difficult. To land a top job, you need to be clear about the distinct value you bring to the role you want. Yet the higher you rise, the harder it becomes to get honest opinions about your strengths and weaknesses. In Show Up to Win , Kelly O. Kay and Jeff Sanders, partners at executive search and consulting firm Heidrick & Struggles, lay out a road map to help you win that top-level role and move into it effectively. Backed by a wealth of insights from real-life case studies and interviews, this straight-talking book shows what the job search looks like for today's senior-level candidates, what companies are looking for in candidates for their top jobs, and how you can identify and best position yourself to win the role they've defined. Drawing on more than three decades of experience and two hundred conversations per week with Fortune 1000 companies about executive roles, the authors highlight unexpected perspectives and counterintuitive advice on what differentiates the candidates who land the best jobs from those who are overlooked because they fail to distinguish themselves at the highest levels. The result is a deeply practical and timeless exploration of how you should think about and navigate a high-stakes executive job search.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3"]', '#CardInstancef3437pW9ruOPtU14WoClmw')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_

Are you a purpose-driven entrepreneur, consultant, or creative who wants to grow online—without becoming someone you’re not? Do you feel too camera-shy, time-poor, or tech-timid to keep up with the social media chaos? This book is for you. title: Just Show Up: The Dance of Walking through Suffering Together
description: Kara Tippetts's story was not a story of disease, although she lost her battle with terminal cancer. It was not a story of saying goodbye, although she was intentional in her time with her husband and four children. Kara's story was one of seeing God in the hard and in the good. It was one of finding grace in the everyday. And it was one of knowing "God with us" through fierce and beautiful friendship. In Just Show Up , Kara and her close friend, Jill Lynn Buteyn, write about what friendship looks like in the midst of changing life seasons, loads of laundry, and even cancer. Whether you are eager to be present to someone going through a difficult time or simply want inspiration for pursuing friends in a new way, this eloquent and practical book explores the gift of silence, the art of receiving, and what it means to just show up. The late Kara Tippetts was the author of The Hardest Peace and blogged faithfully at mundanefaithfulness.com. Cancer was only a part of Kara's story. Her real fight was to truly live while facing a crushing reality. Since her death in March 2015, her husband, Jason, is parenting their four children and leading the church they founded in Colorado Springs, Colorado. Jill Lynn Buteyn lives in Colorado with her husband and two children. She has a bachelor's degree in communications from Bethel University. title: Just Show Up: And Other Enduring Values from Baseball's Iron Man
description: In this New York Times–bestselling guide to success, the nineteen-time All-Star and World Series–winning legend shares his values and principles for the game of life, drawn from lessons he learned on and off the field. On September six, 1995, Cal Ripken Jr. played his two,131st consecutive game in Major League Baseball, breaking Lou Gehrig's Iron Man streak (he would go on to play another 501 consecutive games) and capping a career that included helping to deliver the 1983 World Series victory to his beloved Baltimore. Ripken is a baseball legend, and the son of revered coach Cal Ripken Sr.—but legends aren't born; they're made. Ripken Jr.'s keynotes were his consistency, hard work, and loyalty—in more than twenty years as a major leaguer, he only ever played for the Orioles. There were successes and failures, but beyond it all was the old-fashioned sense of doing what was right, every single day. Since his retirement, Ripken has parlayed his fame into a successful post-baseball career as a television analyst, youth baseball entrepreneur, and author. In Just Show Up , he uses all these experiences to create a vision for a better life. His core values remain age-old: "Have a mentor, and be one, too"; "Success and money are not the same"; and "Play fair—win fair." Sprinkled throughout are firsthand accounts of his legendary father; fellow superstar baseball players and the games they played; what it was like to keep the streak alive; what it meant to bring the World Series to Baltimore; and simple yet poignant takeaways for anyone trying to forge a successful life in these often chaotic times. title: Show Up: The Five Steps To Getting Out Of Your Own Way
description: Don’t sweat the small stuff. OBSESS over the small stuff. Anthony Melchiorri started his hospitality career working as at the Embassy Suites in Overland Park, Kansas, and worked his way up to becoming one of the most successful general managers in New York City. During the process, he discovered the five steps that allowed him to show up for himself and for the hotels and owners in which he served. Then, in 2012, he landed a deal with the Travel Channel that saw him host nine seasons of Hotel Impossible . He used these five steps to help other hoteliers turn around their establishments. Melchiorri’s sometimes humorous, sometimes serious stories highlight how these five steps can work for people from all walks of life, whether those people are future hospitality experts or digital nomads. The stories are packed with takeaways and insights and give a glimpse into the unwavering mindset of the man behind the suit and tie. Show Up: The 5 Steps To Getting Out Of Your Own Way lays out the path that you can walk to create a professional life that reflects who you are and what you value. “Through the artful weaving of relatable stories and practical advice, Show Up leaves readers feeling both enlightened and empowered. As a former hotel executive, Anthony possesses remarkable empathy for others that shines through every page, making this an absolute must-read for anyone seeking to take charge of their life and live it to the fullest.” - Robert H. title: Show Up and Shimmy: Discover Your Worth, Recognize Your Potential, and Lead the Life You D
description: A deeply human narrative of healing, sobriety, and achievement in the face of adversity In Show Up and Shimmy: Discover Your Worth, Recognize Your Potential, and Lead the Life You Deserve , certified motivational speaker Bruce Brackett delivers a stirring narrative that reminds us of what we’re worth, the value we bring to the world, and our unique ability to engage with the people we care about. The book combines the straightforward, effective affirmations Brackett is known for with an unflinching and realistic look at the challenges he’s faced throughout his life – and how he meets them head-on every day. Show Up and Shimmy offers simple, grounded slogans that remind you to focus on the positive and “Keep Moving Forward,” even when life seems intent on doing everything it can to stop you. It offers a compelling argument for the idea that – regardless of how difficult or intimidating your circumstances are right now – there is a way forward, it is achievable, and you are worth every bit of the effort it will take . title: SHOW UP AND STAND OUT: STEP UP. SHOW OUT. BE UNFORGETTABLE
description: Stop shrinking in rooms you were meant to lead. Are you the best-kept secret in your industry? You have the credentials, the work ethic, and the results, yet you find yourself being passed over for promotions, talked over in meetings, or invisible in a crowded marketplace. Skill is rarely the problem—the problem is legibility . If the room can’t read your value the moment you walk in, you’ve already lost the lead. In Show Up and Stand Out , executive coach and personal branding strategist Wil Gravely-Strayhorn reveals that presence isn’t an innate gift for the charismatic few; it is a high-level skill that anyone can master. The P.O.I.S.E.™ Framework for Unforgettable Presence Moving beyond superficial "hacks," Gravely-Strayhorn introduces his proprietary P.O.I.S.E.™ Method —a deep-dive into the five pillars of professional identity development: Perception: Close the gap between how you see yourself and how the room receives you. Optimization: Align your body language, energy, and visual signal to match your message. Identity: Own your story and values to build a brand anchored in radical self-trust. Strategy: Stop guessing and start showing up on purpose in the places that matter. Execution: Develop the habits and mindset to remain consistent when the pressure is on. Whether you are a mid-career professional repositioning for the C-suite, a BIPOC leader navigating corporate nuances, or an entrepreneur building a legacy, this book provides the roadmap to stop blending in. With 76 actionable chapters, you will learn to overcome imposter syndrome, master non-verbal communication, and build a "legible" brand that carries your name into rooms you haven’t even entered yet.
